items.t: Killarney is an official City of Vancouver local area (one of the City's 22) in the southeastern corner of the city, bordering Burnaby across Boundary Road to the east and the Fraser River to the south, with Champlain Heights inside it and the Fraserlands along the river. "Killarney VE" is the board sub-area name for the same area.

Where the condo stock concentrates: almost entirely at the south edge, in the River District (East Fraser Lands) waterfront — Sawmill Crescent, River District Crossing, Riverwalk Avenue, Rivergrass Drive and East Kent Avenue, north of SE Marine Drive / Marine Way. The established streets and Champlain Heights are primarily single-family homes, townhouse complexes and co-op / leasehold housing — the City describes Killarney as primarily single-family residential, with some multi-family homes, and highrises in the recently developed Fraserlands.
Main roads serving the area: Kerr Street, Rupert Street, East 41st Avenue, East 49th Avenue and SE Marine Drive / Marine Way.

Transit: there is no SkyTrain station inside Killarney. Route 49 runs Metrotown Station to UBC via 49th Avenue; route 26 serves the area to Joyce Station; route 100 runs Marpole Loop to 22nd Street Station via Marine Drive.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Killarney

items.t: Area plan: the East Fraser Lands Official Development Plan (River District) applies at the south edge — a mainly residential community with a variety of housing types and a commercial centre on the former Canadian White Pine Sawmill site, with Wesgroup Properties owning the majority of the land; Area 1, Area 2 and Kerr Street have been rezoned with ODP / CD-1 amendments enacted.

blocks.text: Good to know about Killarney

items.t: One developer built most of what you can buy. Wesgroup owns the majority of the East Fraser Lands and built the Town Centre buildings, the Avalon Park buildings, MODE and Paradigm; Polygon built Currents, New Water and Rhythm. Cross-building comparisons of construction and warranty in River District are unusually direct because the builder set is so small.

The district sits on a sawmill site, and the newest neighbour is non-market. The East Fraser Lands ODP covers the former Canadian White Pine Sawmill site, and the 337-unit Sawmill Housing Development (rental + co-op) has now opened inside the district — the tenure mix is part of the plan, not an anomaly.

Champlain Heights' leases expire in the 2080s. The majority of Champlain Heights is pre-paid 99-year City leasehold — a fact that does not appear in a quick listing read, and that changes financing, depreciation and resale analysis completely versus the freehold River District strata a few blocks south.

One Town Centre answers to two addresses. The developer markets 8550 River District Crossing, while MLS® sale records address One Town Centre units at 3557 Sawmill Crescent (Strata Plan EPS4966). Confirm which address a unit's title and strata records use before ordering documents.

Killarney Community Centre is the amenity anchor away from the river. At 6260 Killarney Street, it has an indoor pool, ice rink and fitness centre, with Killarney Park beside it — the established part of Killarney is served independently of the River District's Club Central.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Killarney

items.t: Form B diligence (Park Place, and any strata unit in the carried River District developments): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

blocks.text: Good to know about Killarney

items.t: Killarney was forest and farms until after WWII. The City's history records that the area remained second-growth forest and farms until after the war, and that the first non-native settler, William Rowling (1868), came to own 3.5 kilometres of Fraser River shoreline including all of Killarney's riverfront — which is why the house stock is post-war and the waterfront is all new.

The community centre is the area's real amenity anchor. Killarney Community Centre, 6260 Killarney Street, has an indoor pool, ice rink and fitness centre with Killarney Park beside it — and Park Place's townhomes sit on the same East 49th Avenue corridor, a fact listing copy rarely connects.

Everett Crowley Park is a former landfill turned forest park. At 8200 Kerr Street, the City describes 40 hectares of walking trails and an off-leash dog area (the Park Board dataset figure is 38.08 hectares) — the big green space on Killarney's east side is a rehabilitated site, not old-growth.

The River District sits on a sawmill site. The East Fraser Lands plan area is the former Canadian White Pine Sawmill site, and Wesgroup Properties owns the majority of the land — one developer's phasing decisions drive nearly all of the area's new attached supply, townhouses included.

The library serving Killarney carries the other neighbourhood's name. The Vancouver Public Library branch for the area is the Champlain Heights Branch at 7110 Kerr Street — a small sign of how completely the two names interleave on the ground, even though the board places them as separate sub-areas.
Health care runs through Knight Street, not a Killarney hospital.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Killarney
Fee-simple lots

items.t: House lots: the City describes Killarney as primarily single-family residential, with some multi-family homes, and highrises in the recently developed Fraserlands. The established streets and Champlain Heights' freehold pockets are freehold detached houses under the R1-1 District Schedule. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.

Lot character: R1-1 minimum site areas run from 306 m² (single detached house or duplex) through 464 m² (multiple dwelling with 5 units) to 557 m² (6 to 8 units); a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house, and a multiplex may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units. These are schedule minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel.

Serviced position: Killarney homes are on City water and sewer services; a 2026 utility dollar figure for a Killarney house confirmed on a City source is not verified. Servicing for any specific subdivision or multiplex proposal is confirmed with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: ALR land inside Killarney is not verified — no ALR parcel is confirmed and no split is stated.

Flood position: the City's designated floodplain includes the coastal floodplain along the Fraser River in South Vancouver, and land in the floodplain is subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for setbacks and flood construction levels — this applies to the Fraserlands / River District foreshore. Whether a specific Killarney parcel is in the floodplain is not verified parcel by parcel.

blocks.text: Development land

items.t: The landholding: the East Fraser Lands Official Development Plan (River District) applies at the south edge — a mainly residential community with a variety of housing types and a commercial centre on the former Canadian White Pine Sawmill site, with Wesgroup Properties owning the majority of the land; Area 1, Area 2 and Kerr Street have been rezoned with Official Development Plan / CD-1 amendments enacted. The unbuilt balance of this land is one developer's phased development land — it is not subdivided into lots for public sale, and no bare-lot offering within it was verified.

What a buyer actually buys there: The district's tenure mix is part of the plan: the Sawmill Housing Development (337 homes — 220 non-profit rentals operated by M'akola Housing Society and 117 co-op homes with Community Land Trust) is rental and co-operative housing on district land, not sale stock.
A specific current presale project in the district verified on a developer site: Not verified: — future River District phases are documented here as plan build-out only, never as for-sale inventory.

blocks.text: Leasehold ground

items.t: The majority of Champlain Heights is leasehold property — pre-paid 99-year leases from the City of Vancouver expiring in the 2080s: A home there sits on City land under a prepaid lease: there is no fee-simple lot to buy, financing and resale run on the remaining lease term, and there is no strata Form B for a co-op or leasehold purchase. Per-complex tenure must be read off title — at least one Champlain Heights complex (Marine Woods) has listing evidence calling a unit a rare freehold townhouse, so the area's general leasehold reputation must never be blanket-applied to a specific complex.

items.t: Main roads: Kerr Street, Rupert Street, East 41st Avenue, East 49th Avenue and SE Marine Drive / Marine Way. Transit: there is no SkyTrain station inside Killarney — route 49 runs Metrotown Station to UBC via 49th Avenue, route 26 serves the area to Joyce Station, and route 100 runs Marpole Loop to 22nd Street Station via Marine Drive.

Civic anchors: Killarney Community Centre, 6260 Killarney Street (indoor pool, ice rink, fitness centre), with Killarney Park beside it; Vancouver Public Library Champlain Heights Branch, 7110 Kerr Street; Everett Crowley Park, 8200 Kerr Street — the City describes 40 hectares with walking trails and an off-leash area (the Park Board dataset figure is 38.08 hectares). blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Killarney

items.t: Zoning — Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575: the house streets sit under the R1-1 District Schedule, while East Fraser Lands parcels are under site-specific CD-1 districts — for example CD-1 (566), East Fraser Lands Town Square Precinct (By-law No. 10941), and CD-1 (567), East Fraser Lands Waterfront Precinct (By-law No. 10943), each an amendment to By-law No. 3575.

Plan — East Fraser Lands Official Development Plan (River District): the governing plan for the south-edge land, as documented in — a mainly residential community with a commercial centre on the former sawmill site, Wesgroup owning the majority of the land, with Area 1, Area 2 and Kerr Street rezoned by enacted ODP / CD-1 amendments. Land outside the district follows the citywide framework and the R1-1 schedule.

Floodplain standards: the designated floodplain covers the Fraser River frontage, and parcels in it carry Vancouver Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements — for River District land this is a design condition of the district itself, and for any specific parcel the City dataset governs.

Leasehold diligence (Champlain Heights ground): a prepaid 99-year City lease expiring in the 2080s is valued on its remaining term, not as fee-simple land; confirm the lease's rent/prepayment status, assignment and financing terms on title before comparing any Champlain Heights price to a freehold Killarney lot, and verify the specific complex's tenure — the freehold exception noted in means title, not neighbourhood reputation, decides.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Killarney ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

blocks.text: Good to know about Killarney

items.t: The River District sits on a sawmill site, and one owner phases it: the East Fraser Lands plan area is the former Canadian White Pine Sawmill site and Wesgroup Properties owns the majority of the land — one developer's phasing decisions drive nearly all new supply at Killarney's south edge, and the "land market" there is that phasing, not lot sales.

Killarney was forest and farms until after WWII: the City records that the area remained second-growth forest and farms until after the war, and that the first non-native settler, William Rowling (1868), came to own 3.5 kilometres of Fraser River shoreline including all of Killarney's riverfront — which is why the house stock is post-war and the only comprehensively-planned ground is the old sawmill land.

Everett Crowley Park was a landfill: the roughly 40-hectare park at 8200 Kerr Street is Champlain Heights' green core and a former city landfill — relevant context for lots on its edge, and part of why the Champlain Heights ground was planned as one community in the 1970s rather than sold lot by lot.

One Town Centre answers to two addresses: the developer markets 8550 River District Crossing, while MLS® sale records address One Town Centre units at 3557 Sawmill Crescent (Strata Plan EPS4966) — confirm which address a unit's title and strata records use before ordering documents; the same dual-address habit is what keeps Avalon Mews mis-filed between two sub-areas.

The library serving Killarney carries the other neighbourhood's name: the Vancouver Public Library branch for the area is the Champlain Heights Branch at 7110 Kerr Street — a small sign of how completely the City's "inside Killarney" geography and the board's separate sub-area interleave on the same ground.

faq.a: In the River District at the Fraser River edge — Sawmill Crescent, River District Crossing, Riverwalk Avenue, Rivergrass Drive and East Kent Avenue. The rest of Killarney (the house streets and Champlain Heights) has no verified freehold strata apartment buildings in the sources checked.

Usually not in the freehold sense: Champlain Heights consists mainly of townhouse complexes and co-op housing, and the majority of the area is leasehold — pre-paid 99-year City of Vancouver leases expiring in the 2080s. There is no strata Form B for a co-op or leasehold purchase; get leasehold-specific advice.
faq.q: Is a Champlain Heights home a strata condo?

faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, and the published lines for this area's buildings (rentals allowed at 8533 River District Crossing; rentals allowed with restrictions at Two Town Centre) are consistent with that. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax declaration still applies if the unit sits empty.
faq.q: Can I rent out a River District condo?

faq.a: The designated floodplain covers the Fraser River frontage, and parcels in it carry Vancouver Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements.
